results.title: How To | Track & Bus Routing in Playback
results.summary: Bus routing and MultiOuts require a Playback Premium subscription. Playback groups 150+ instruments into 16 buses plus a dedicated SMPTE bus; each bus can go to any available output on the selected audio device, mono or stereo. The Pad bus cannot be re-routed. Track routing is saved per device and applies globally to that track; it is not saved with setlists or named arrangements.

steps.text: Route tracks to buses: Settings > Tracks tab, assign each track to a bus (defaults are preset and can be overwritten).
Route buses to outputs: Settings > Buses tab, tap a bus row and choose an available output.
Route several buses at once: tap 'Assign Multiple Busses' in the bottom-right, select buses, assign one output.
Rename a bus: drag its row to the left to reveal Edit.
Greyed-out output: the SMPTE bus is probably using it. Disable SMPTE in the General tab or set the SMPTE bus to 'None'.

Alternative from the main interface: open the 'Busses' layer (bottom right next to the master fader, or cycle layers with the button beside it), tap Edit (top right) to enter Setlist/Song Map edit mode, tap a bus name and select the output.
Bus mixes are song-specific by default; disable Song Specific Buses in Settings for a global mix. Solo/mute on a bus affects all tracks routed to it.

results.title: How To | Route Click & Guide to Separate Busses in Playback (legacy, pre-7.6)
results.summary: The article itself states these steps are no longer relevant for Playback 7.6 and newer, where Click and Guide are separated by default. Kept for the routing pattern: rename a spare bus, move Guide tracks to it in Settings > Tracks, then assign each bus to an interface output in Settings > Buses. Buses require a Playback Pro (Premium) subscription and an interface with more than 2 outputs.

steps.text: Free up a bus: swipe left on the Aux bus, tap Edit, rename it to 'Guide'. Then in Settings > Tracks move any instrument parts still routed to it to another bus (tap the cell, choose a bus, tap Done).
In the Tracks tab, move Guide (Dynamic) and Guide (Non-Dynamic) out of the Click & Guide bus into the Guide bus.
In Settings > Buses, tap the Click and Guide bus cells and select an output for each (example: Click to output 1, Guide to output 2).

results.title: Playback General Settings Overview
results.summary: Lists every setting in the General tab (three-line menu icon top-right > General). Audio-relevant items: Auto-Pan, Click Sound, Song Specific Buses (Premium), Audio Device (shows and sets which connected device Playback uses for all audio output), Power Saver, MIDI Out, and SMPTE Timecode. The page gives no detail on Audio Device choices and does not mention sample rate, Bluetooth, storage, or subscription display.

steps.text: Open settings: tap the three-line menu icon in the top-right corner of Playback and make sure the General tab is selected.
Audio Device: shows and sets which connected audio device Playback uses for all audio output.
Auto-Pan: routes click and guide to the left mono output and all tracks to the right mono output of the device's stereo output.
Song Specific Buses (Premium): on gives each song its own bus fader mix; off uses one global bus mix.
Power Saver: improves performance on older devices; disables fader VU meters and fader multi-touch and reduces waveform scrolling feedback.
MIDI Out: enabled by default; disable if unused to improve performance and battery life.
SMPTE Timecode: toggles SMPTE output and selects frame rate.
Fader Default Level at 80%: on presets faders to 80% for headroom; off loads tracks at 100%.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Playback Settings > Buses Settings Tab
results.text:
Bus Outputs

The Bus Settings tab is where Buses can be customized and outputs can be re-routed. Playback has 16 default buses with default SmartRouting that automatically route the related instrument tracks to each of the buses. However, Bus routing and naming is completely customizable and saved by audio device.

Quick Tip: Renaming Playback Buses in Bus Settings

- Swipe Left on any bus cell to Edit the name and abbreviation
- Name: Change the name of a Playback bus
- Abbreviation: Change the bus name shown under the fader in the Buses mixer
- Emojis are supported for bus names 😉

Note: For an in-depth overview of Playback bus routing and features, see:
​📖Bus Routing in Playback

Change Bus Routing

Bus Routing is saved and recalled based on the connected audio device and dependent on the number of supported outputs. If an audio interface has 10 outputs, then those 16 are available for routing.

- Tap the bus cell to open the routing menu
- Choose which output to route the bus to and press Done

Note: if a particular output is greyed-out, it's possible that the SMPTE bus is enabled and routed to that output. Either change the SMPTE output routing, or disable SMPTE output from the General Settings Tab if not intending to use it.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Playback Settings > Tracks Settings Tab
results.text:
Tracks Outputs

The Tracks Settings tab is where the default bus routing of every instrument part in the MultiTracks.com catalog can be adjusted. Scroll to any instrument part, Tap the row, and select the new bus that this track will be routed to.

Track routing in Playback is device specific, and is global for that track. So changing the routing for a track name "Electric guitar 3" will change that track's routing across all songs and setlists on that device.

· Auto Pan: Send click and tracks from Playback using the headphone port without any additional audio hardware. Learn how to use Auto Pan with Playback.

· MultiOuts: With a Premium subscription, Playback can send up to 32 outputs can be accessed using compatible audio devices.
